dedupe_keys.name: lscs cf public space conditions and the formation of local sports communities

description: LSCs-CF is an agent-based model of how conditions of a public space shape whether local sports communities form in high-mobility cities. A small group already exercises in an abstract, configurable space, and the model asks how strangers join and whether the loose gathering becomes a stable community. Three conditions each act through one channel: spatial legibility decides whether a passer-by notices the activity, routine compatibility whether a member attends in a week, and social anchor availability how much one meeting builds a tie. Across 32,790 runs in eight experiments it finds two thresholds along routine compatibility, one for survival and one for consolidation, with a wide band where a space is used but no community forms. It was published by Yijia Jiang on CoMSES in August 2026, release 1.1.0. Coverage: abstract public space. Access: free NetLogo code on CoMSES. Licence: MIT. Caveats: abstract; not calibrated to a real site. Simulation uses are testing designs and programming of parks and squares for sustained community use. Related records: MUGS and the Krakow sport facility location model.
